title: The Ultimate Chocolate Mud Cake
description: A decadent, dense, and fudgy masterpiece topped with silky chocolate ganache — the ultimate indulgence.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 150°C fan-forced or 160°C standard. Grease and line a 23 cm springform cake tin, extending the baking paper 5 cm above the rim.

Place 250 g unsalted butter and 200 g of the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Microwave for 1 minute on high, stir, then microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring between each, until smooth and glossy.
Add both sugars and coffee. Stir in 375 ml of the full-cream milk, eggs, and vanilla extract until combined.
Sift in plain flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt. Stir until smooth and fully combined.
Pour batter into the prepared tin and bake for 80–90 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out with moist crumbs. Avoid opening the oven door early.
Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the ganache: combine the remaining 60 ml of milk and 60 ml thickened cream in a jug and microwave for approximately 1 minute until hot but not boiling.
Pour over the remaining 200 g of finely chopped dark chocolate. Let sit for 5 minutes, then stir until smooth. Reheat briefly in 10-second bursts if needed.
Level the cooled cake with a serrated knife if needed, then pour ganache over the top and spread evenly.
Refrigerate for approximately 2 hours or until the ganache is firm. Can also set at room temperature if cool enough.
Slice and serve — the cake is even fudgier on the second day.

notes.title: Mud Cake Texture
notes.content: The skewer should come out with moist crumbs, not clean. A clean skewer means the cake is overbaked and will be dry rather than fudgy. Do not open the oven door during the first hour of baking.

notes.title: Tall Parchment
notes.content: Extending the baking paper 6 cm above the tin rim prevents the crust from burning during the long bake and makes lifting the cake out easier.

notes.title: Serving Tip
notes.content: This cake improves with time. Make it a day ahead — the crumb becomes denser and more fudgy overnight in the refrigerator.
